comments.text: The RCCS duct group rests on a shared cavity environment and shared make, so SY-B3 needs the grouping basis closed against the DA-D8 parameter set before the alpha factors are final.
The protection logic carries a single software image across the trip and isolation functions, so SY-B11 needs the software common cause modeled rather than left as a bounding term.
A 4 hour battery against a 24 hour mission needs the load-shedding calculation closed under SY-B12, since the current model assumes the duty without showing it.
Two RCCS duct groups share the cavity riser, so SY-B8 needs the riser-level dependent failure confirmed in the fault tree, not only noted in the text.
The screening of the indicating lamps and root valves is clean and each exclusion cites a stated criterion.
comments.resolution: No change required, the screening criteria are applied consistently.

systemDefinitions.name: Reactor protection system
systemDefinitions.description: RPS fails to trip the reactor on demand
boundaries: Flux and process sensors
Two trip divisions
Reserve shutdown and rod insertion

diagrams.title: Figure 2-8. Safety protection subsystem functional overview
diagrams.filename: Plant protection and instrumentation system design description

systemDefinitions.successCriterion: One of two divisions trips the reactor, or the negative temperature feedback caps power at 5 percent of nominal.

alignments.name: Both divisions in service
alignments.description: Either division trips the reactor, with the rods held at the power position.

alignments.name: One division bypassed for testing
alignments.description: The remaining division must trip alone while the other is under surveillance.

justificationForExclusionOfComponents: Spurious reactor trip, which shuts the plant down rather than defeating the trip.
Control rods dropping in without a trip demand, which adds negative reactivity and helps the function.
flowDiversionConsiderations: None. The protection system carries signals and rods, not a process fluid.
functionLossConditions: Cabinet temperature above the qualified limit after a long loss of room cooling, which can drift the trip setpoints.
testAndMaintenanceProcedures: Quarterly channel functional test, one division at a time
Rod drop timing test at each refueling outage
operatingLimitations: One trip division may be bypassed for no more than 6 hours for testing.
systemDefinitions.preOperationalInformationJustification: Models from the design package, to confirm by walkdown when as-built.

systemDefinitions.name: Shutdown cooling system
systemDefinitions.description: Shutdown cooling fails to remove core heat for the mission time
boundaries: Two shutdown-cooling circulators
Shutdown heat exchangers
Cooling-water and Class 1E supplies

diagrams.title: Fig. 4-13. Shutdown cooling system arrangement

systemDefinitions.successCriterion: Two of two trains start within 33 hours at full power, one of two in the other states.

alignments.name: Both trains in standby
alignments.description: Circulators stopped and shutdown coolers filled, ready for an automatic start.

alignments.name: One train out of service for maintenance
alignments.description: The remaining train must start and run alone.

justificationForExclusionOfComponents: A single-train overcool, which lowers core temperatures and helps the function.
A spurious circulator start, which starts cooling early and helps the function.
flowDiversionConsiderations: Helium bypassing the core through the idle train when only one train runs. The idle circulator's shutoff valve blocks this path, and its failure is part of the circulator failure data.
functionLossConditions: Cooling-water supply above its design temperature, which cuts the shutdown cooler duty below the decay heat.
Circulator motor room above its qualified temperature after a ventilation loss.
testAndMaintenanceProcedures: Monthly circulator start test on each train
Shutdown cooler inspection and cleaning each outage
operatingLimitations: One shutdown-cooling train may be out of service for up to 7 days at power.
operatingProcedures: Loss of forced cooling response procedure
systemDefinitions.preOperationalInformationJustification: Models from the design package, to confirm by walkdown when as-built.

systemDefinitions.name: Reactor cavity cooling system
systemDefinitions.description: Cavity cooling fails to carry the conduction cooldown
boundaries: Four natural-draft duct groups
Cavity cooling panels
Common intake and exhaust stack

diagrams.title: Figure 2-17. Schematic RCCS airflow blockage location for failure modes and effects analysis
diagrams.filename: Reactor cavity cooling system design description

systemDefinitions.successCriterion: The passive ducts carry at least half the nominal capacity at power, a quarter shut down.

alignments.name: All four duct groups open
alignments.description: Natural draft through every duct group, with no active component to start.

alignments.name: One duct group isolated for inspection
alignments.description: Three duct groups still carry more than half of the nominal capacity.

justificationForExclusionOfComponents: Overcooling from excess draft, which lowers cavity temperatures and helps the function.
flowDiversionConsiderations: Cold inlet air short-circuiting into the hot outlet plenum through a failed plenum seal, which bypasses the cooling panels. It is counted in the duct group blockage events.
functionLossConditions: Outdoor air above the design temperature, which lowers the natural draft and the heat removal.
Snow, ice or debris over the inlet and outlet structures in a severe winter storm.
testAndMaintenanceProcedures: Quarterly walkdown of the inlet and outlet screens
Panel thermocouple calibration each outage
operatingLimitations: No more than one duct group may be isolated at power.
operatingProcedures: Cavity cooling panel temperature monitoring procedure
Duct inlet and outlet clearing procedure after external events
systemDefinitions.preOperationalInformationJustification: Models from the design package, to confirm by walkdown when as-built.

systemDefinitions.name: Steam-generator isolation and dump
systemDefinitions.description: Steam-generator isolation and dump fails on a moisture alarm
boundaries: Steam and feedwater isolation valves
Steam-generator dump path
Moisture-detection interface

diagrams.title: Fig. 4-17. Steam and water dump subsystem schematic

systemDefinitions.successCriterion: The affected steam generator isolates and dumps within 2 hours of the moisture alarm.

alignments.name: Both loops in service
alignments.description: Isolation valves open and the dump valve closed on both loops.

alignments.name: One loop shut down with its steam generator isolated
alignments.description: The isolated loop cannot admit water into the primary circuit.
alignments.justificationIfNotModeled: The isolated loop is already in its safe end state, so it cannot defeat the function.

justificationForExclusionOfComponents: Spurious isolation of a healthy loop, which stops that loop but does not defeat the isolation of the leaking one. The initiating event analysis covers it as a loss of the heat sink.
flowDiversionConsiderations: None. The dump drains to the dump tank through a dedicated line with no branch.
functionLossConditions: Dump tank back pressure above the design value, which slows the drain past the 2-hour window.
testAndMaintenanceProcedures: Quarterly isolation valve stroke test
Dump valve seat leakage test each outage
operatingLimitations: Isolation and dump must complete within 2 hours of a moisture alarm.
systemDefinitions.preOperationalInformationJustification: Models from the design package, to confirm by walkdown when as-built.

systemDefinitions.name: Helium boundary isolation
systemDefinitions.description: Helium boundary isolation fails to isolate the leaking segment
boundaries: Segment isolation valves
Interfacing-system boundary valves
Leak-detection interface

diagrams.title: Fig. 4-18. Pressure relief subsystem schematic

systemDefinitions.successCriterion: The leaking helium segment or interfacing line is isolated at its boundary valves before the inventory reaches the depressurized band.

alignments.name: Boundary valves open for normal service
alignments.description: Every segment and interfacing line is open and pressurized.

alignments.name: Interfacing line isolated for maintenance
alignments.description: The isolated line removes one leak path and one isolation demand.

justificationForExclusionOfComponents: Spurious isolation of a healthy segment, which closes the boundary without a leak and does not defeat the function.
flowDiversionConsiderations: None. Each segment has isolation valves at every penetration, so no unisolated branch remains.
functionLossConditions: Hot helium discharged into the reactor building, which heats the valve actuators past their qualified temperature.
testAndMaintenanceProcedures: Boundary valve stroke and seat leakage test each outage
operatingLimitations: A leaking segment must be isolated before the inventory reaches the depressurized band.
systemDefinitions.preOperationalInformationJustification: Models from the design package, to confirm by walkdown when as-built.

systemDefinitions.name: Depressurization and leak detection
systemDefinitions.description: Detection fails to alarm on a falling helium pressure
boundaries: Redundant primary pressure channels
Leak and activity monitors
Control-room alarm and indication

diagrams.title: Figure 2-5. Simplified block diagram, primary coolant pumpdown
diagrams.filename: Plant protection and instrumentation system design description

systemDefinitions.successCriterion: Redundant pressure and leak instrumentation alarms so operators diagnose a depressurization and act.

alignments.name: All channels in service
alignments.description: Both pressure channels and the activity monitors feed the control-room alarm.

alignments.name: One pressure channel bypassed for calibration
alignments.description: The remaining channel and the activity monitors must detect the depressurization.

justificationForExclusionOfComponents: Spurious alarm, which prompts an unnecessary but safe operator response.
flowDiversionConsiderations: None. The detection channels carry signals, not a process fluid.
functionLossConditions: Hot helium discharged into the reactor building, which drifts the pressure transmitters past their accuracy band.
testAndMaintenanceProcedures: Pressure channel calibration every 18 months
Monthly alarm annunciation test
operatingLimitations: One pressure channel may be bypassed for no more than 8 hours.
systemDefinitions.preOperationalInformationJustification: Models from the design package, to confirm by walkdown when as-built.

systemDefinitions.name: Helium inventory and pressure control
systemDefinitions.description: Helium inventory control fails to restore pressure
boundaries: Helium make-up compressor and storage
Pressure-control valves
Purification interface

diagrams.title: Fig. 4-28. Helium storage and transfer subsystem flow diagram

systemDefinitions.successCriterion: The make-up path restores helium inventory, or the slow depressurization proceeds to conduction cooldown.

alignments.name: Make-up compressor in standby
alignments.description: Storage pressurized and the control valves closed, ready for make-up.

alignments.name: Purification train aligned for clean-up
alignments.description: Part of the inventory flows through the purification train.
alignments.justificationIfNotModeled: Purification does not change the make-up path the success criterion credits.

justificationForExclusionOfComponents: Overpressure, which the relief path limits and which does not threaten the criterion.
A spurious make-up start, which adds helium and helps restore pressure.
flowDiversionConsiderations: Make-up helium flowing to the purification system instead of the primary circuit. The purification isolation valve closes on the make-up signal, and its failure is part of the pressure-control valve event.
functionLossConditions: Compressor room above its qualified temperature after a ventilation loss.
testAndMaintenanceProcedures: Monthly compressor start test
Storage pressure check each shift
operatingLimitations: Storage must hold enough helium to restore the design inventory once.
systemDefinitions.preOperationalInformationJustification: Models from the design package, to confirm by walkdown when as-built.

systemDefinitions.name: Reactor building isolation and filtration
systemDefinitions.description: The reactor building fails to isolate or filter on demand
boundaries: Building isolation dampers
Filtered ventilation trains
Isolation actuation signal
systemDefinitions.successCriterion: The reactor building isolates on demand and holds the design leak rate with filtration.

alignments.name: One filtration train running
alignments.description: The second train is in standby and the isolation dampers are open.

alignments.name: Both filtration trains stopped for a ventilation outage
alignments.description: Building ventilation is shut down for planned work.
alignments.justificationIfNotModeled: Allowed only in cold shutdown with the helium depressurized, so no release path needs filtering.

justificationForExclusionOfComponents: Premature isolation, which closes the boundary earlier than needed.
flowDiversionConsiderations: Leakage through an unisolated building penetration, which bypasses the filters. The design leak rate in the success criterion covers it.
functionLossConditions: Graphite dust loading the filters past the fan capacity, which cuts the filtered flow.
testAndMaintenanceProcedures: Quarterly damper closure timing test
Filter efficiency test every 18 months
operatingLimitations: One filtration train may be out of service for up to 7 days.
systemDefinitions.preOperationalInformationJustification: Models from the design package, to confirm by walkdown when as-built.

systemDefinitions.name: Non-Class 1E AC power
systemDefinitions.description: Non-Class 1E AC power fails to supply the shutdown-cooling loads after a loss of normal power
boundaries: Two backup gas-turbine generators in the standby power building
4160 V energy conversion area buses and the bus tie between units
480 V unit substations and motor control centers feeding the shutdown-cooling loads

diagrams.title: Fig. 4-29. Overall plant medium voltage non-Class 1E AC distribution subsystem

systemDefinitions.successCriterion: Either backup gas-turbine generator, through the bus tie, energizes the energy conversion area buses and the 480 V motor control centers that feed the shutdown-cooling loads for the mission time.

alignments.name: Normal supply from the unit generators
alignments.description: The unit auxiliary transformers feed the buses. Both backup gas-turbine generators are in standby and start when the normal and startup sources are lost.

alignments.name: One backup generator out of service for maintenance
alignments.description: The other backup generator carries the selected investment protection loads of both units through the bus tie.

failureModes: Common cause of the backup generators

justificationForExclusionOfComponents: A spurious backup generator start, which does not interrupt the normal supply.
flowDiversionConsiderations: None. The AC system carries electrical power, not a process fluid.
functionLossConditions: Standby power building above the generators' rated ambient after a ventilation loss, which derates the gas turbines.
testAndMaintenanceProcedures: Periodic backup generator start and load run
Backup generator inspection at each refueling outage
operatingLimitations: Backup generator maintenance is taken one generator at a time, so the bus tie keeps one generator available to both units.
operatingProcedures: Backup generator start and bus tie procedure
systemDefinitions.preOperationalInformationJustification: Models from the design package, to confirm by walkdown when as-built.

systemDefinitions.name: Class 1E DC power
systemDefinitions.description: Class 1E DC power fails to supply the protection and actuation loads
boundaries: Station batteries
DC distribution buses
Battery chargers

diagrams.title: Fig. 4-31. Class 1E DC power system

systemDefinitions.successCriterion: Battery and distribution supply the DC loads for the mission time.

alignments.name: Chargers carry the buses
alignments.description: Batteries float on the chargers and pick up the load on a charger loss.

alignments.name: One charger out of service
alignments.description: Its battery carries the bus until the charger returns.

justificationForExclusionOfComponents: A charger overvoltage trip, which disconnects the charger and leaves the battery carrying the bus.
flowDiversionConsiderations: None. The DC system carries electrical power, not a process fluid.
functionLossConditions: Battery room below the minimum electrolyte temperature in winter, which cuts the battery capacity.
Loads added after the load-shedding calculation, which shorten the battery duty below the mission time.
testAndMaintenanceProcedures: Weekly pilot-cell check
Battery service test at each outage
operatingLimitations: Each battery must carry the protection and actuation loads for the mission time.
systemDefinitions.preOperationalInformationJustification: Models from the design package, to confirm by walkdown when as-built.

systemDefinitions.name: Component cooling water
systemDefinitions.description: Component cooling water fails to cool the shutdown coolers
boundaries: Two cooling-water pumps
Cooling-water heat exchangers
Distribution headers

diagrams.title: Fig. 4-14. Shutdown cooling water subsystem

systemDefinitions.successCriterion: One of two cooling-water trains removes heat from the shutdown coolers.

alignments.name: One pump running, one in standby
alignments.description: The standby pump starts on low header pressure.

alignments.name: Both pumps running for shutdown cooling
alignments.description: Used while both shutdown coolers carry load.

justificationForExclusionOfComponents: Overcooling from excess flow, which lowers the cooler outlet temperature and helps the function.
flowDiversionConsiderations: Cooling water dumped to the drain through a shutdown-cooler relief valve that opens spuriously. It is modeled in each train as CCW-RVA-SO and CCW-RVB-SO.
functionLossConditions: Ultimate heat sink above its design temperature in summer, which cuts the heat removal below the shutdown-cooler duty.
testAndMaintenanceProcedures: Quarterly pump performance test
Heat exchanger cleaning each outage
operatingLimitations: One cooling-water pump may be out of service for up to 7 days.
operatingProcedures: Loss of cooling water response procedure

Isolation-signal interface

alignments.name: One monitor bypassed for calibration

modularizationRecords.justification: Neither part of a division can be recovered once the trip demand passes, and no other system draws on the division logic or its power supply. The rods stay apart because they fail in a different way.
No part of a duct group can be recovered during the cooldown, and no other system uses the ducts. The common stack stays its own event because all four groups need it.

The train is started, run and restored as one unit, so its parts share one recovery potential, and no other system draws on the trains. The isolation dampers stay apart because the isolation function needs them on their own.
The package is restarted as one unit, so its parts share one recovery potential, and its skids serve only their own generator. The output breaker stays apart to match the industry breaker data.

environmentalDesignBasisConsiderations.environmentalConditions: Cavity riser. A depressurization heats the cavity and can degrade two of the four duct groups on the same riser, carried through the environment factor of the duct common cause group.

Shared support cooling. Loss of component cooling water or mechanical support raises the shutdown-cooling room temperature for both trains together, carried as the cooling transfer in the shutdown-cooling fault tree.
Depressurization environment. A blowdown into the building can push the isolation dampers beyond their environmental qualification, so the adverse condition enters as a dependent failure.
Shared battery room. Both battery trains sit in one room, so a room fire or a room heat-up affects both together, carried through the environment factor of the battery common cause group.

componentBoundaryReviews.note: The rod data come from pressurized-water reactor rods. Reflector rods that drop by gravity are outside that population, so the boundary cannot be checked until design-specific data exist.

The generator data count the generator breaker, and the model also carries the output breaker as AC-BKR1-FC and AC-BKR2-FC. The double count is small against the 7.0E-2 start failure and conservative, so it is kept.

The charger event covers a charger fault that the output breaker fails to isolate from the bank. DA still has the charger-to-battery interface under reconciliation (DA-A2), so the boundary stays open until both sides agree.
The monitor estimate comes from nonnuclear instrument records that do not state their boundary. Flagged until vendor data for the monitor are in hand.

modelUncertainties.description: Negative temperature feedback is credited to cap power at about 5 percent of nominal when both divisions fail to trip.
modelUncertainties.impact: Without the credit, both divisions failing would count as a loss of reactivity control and lead to fuel damage in the at-power sequences.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Credited from the passive feedback analysis in the RPS success criterion, and carried as a key assumption into the event sequence quantification.

modelUncertainties.description: Loss of Class 1E DC is modeled as a failure of both trip divisions.
modelUncertainties.impact: If the division logic trips when it loses power, the DC transfer overstates RPS failure.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Kept as a conservative bound until the trip logic power arrangement is fixed in the design.

modelUncertainties.description: Reflector rod insertion uses pressurized-water reactor rod data, flagged under SY-A13.
modelUncertainties.impact: Gravity insertion into reflector channels could fail more or less often than the industry rods, which moves the rod term of RPS failure.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distribution for the rod estimate until design-specific data exist.

ccfUncertainties.description: The division group uses the generic demand factors with staggered testing, with software common cause folded in until the CC-II software model is set (SY-B11).
ccfUncertainties.impact: A separate software common cause event would add a failure path that the hardware factors do not bound.

ccfUncertainties.description: The rod group uses the generic demand factors, since no rod drive template exists.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Rods of one design in one reflector environment could couple more strongly than the industry pool.

dependencyUncertainties.description: Both divisions draw on the DC system through one transfer to its top event, not train by train.
dependencyUncertainties.impact: A failure of one DC train together with a failure of the other division is not modeled, which can understate RPS failure.

modelUncertainties.description: Both trains are needed at full power, from the coupled dynamic campaign (TF-CALC-H01).
modelUncertainties.impact: A one-of-two criterion would remove the single-train failure paths and cut SCS failure at full power.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Tested in the train count sensitivity study.

modelUncertainties.description: Circulator run failures come from gas-cooled test facility experience.
modelUncertainties.impact: A small facility population gives a wide estimate for the risk-significant run failure.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distribution until operating experience exists.

ccfUncertainties.description: The train group uses the compressor fail-to-run factors, updated with one Fort St. Vrain shared cause, with staggered testing.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Helium circulators of one design in one duty may couple more strongly, which would raise the train common cause term.

dependencyUncertainties.description: No credit is taken for restoring AC power within the 33 hour start window.
dependencyUncertainties.impact: Restored offsite or backup power would recover shutdown cooling, so the AC transfer overstates SCS failure.

modelUncertainties.description: The ducts are credited with half the nominal capacity at power and a quarter in the shutdown states, from the passive performance analysis.
modelUncertainties.impact: Weaker natural draft on hot days would lower the number of blocked duct groups that defeats the function.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Performance uncertainty is propagated in the passive system analysis (PST-RCCS).

modelUncertainties.description: Duct and stack blockage come from gas-cooled test facility experience.
modelUncertainties.impact: The stack and the damper misalignment dominate RCCS failure, so a wider stack estimate moves the result most.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distributions.

ccfUncertainties.description: Alpha factors for the four duct groups are the generic rate means, with passive-duct applicability open under DA-D8 (SY-B4).
ccfUncertainties.impact: Coupling between the duct groups sets the three-of-four blockage term, which is a small part of RCCS failure.

dependencyUncertainties.description: Two duct groups share the cavity riser, and the shared-riser failure is not yet in the fault tree (SY-B8).
dependencyUncertainties.impact: A riser failure would block two groups at once and raise the three-of-four term.

modelUncertainties.description: The dump valve must open after isolation for success, from the SC criterion.
modelUncertainties.impact: If isolation alone limits water ingress, the dump valve adds a failure path that overstates SGISO failure.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Kept as the conservative SC criterion.

modelUncertainties.description: Isolation and dump valves use industry data from water and steam service.
modelUncertainties.impact: Valves in the steam generator of a helium plant may fail more or less often.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distributions.

ccfUncertainties.description: The isolation valves on both loops use the main steam isolation valve factors.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Valves of one make tested on one schedule may couple more strongly after a common maintenance error.

dependencyUncertainties.description: Automatic isolation and the operator backup both depend on the moisture monitors.
dependencyUncertainties.impact: A monitor failure removes both paths, so the operator action is not an independent backup.

modelUncertainties.description: Helium isolation valves use industry data from water and steam valves.
modelUncertainties.impact: Helium service seats and seals may fail more or less often than the industry population.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distribution until helium valve data exist.

ccfUncertainties.description: The isolation valve pair uses the motor-operated valve fail-to-close factors.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Valves of one make on one stroke-test schedule may couple more strongly than the generic factor.

dependencyUncertainties.description: The isolation actuation and the operator cue both come from the pressure channels in the detection system.
dependencyUncertainties.impact: A detection failure removes both the automatic isolation and the operator's cue.

modelUncertainties.description: A falling helium pressure is detected by two pressure channels and one alarm, with no credit for other indications.
modelUncertainties.impact: Other plant indications could alert the operators, so the model overstates detection failure.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Conservative. No other indication is credited.

ccfUncertainties.description: The two pressure channels use the generic demand factors and share one calibration practice.
ccfUncertainties.impact: A shared calibration error couples the channels beyond the generic factor.

modelUncertainties.description: Helium storage is modeled as available or unavailable, with no credit for a partial inventory.
modelUncertainties.impact: A partial inventory could still restore pressure in a slow depressurization, so the model overstates HIC failure.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Conservative.

modelUncertainties.description: The make-up compressor uses industry air compressor data.
modelUncertainties.impact: Helium service may change the start failure probability.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distribution.

dependencyUncertainties.description: The operator starts make-up on the low-pressure alarm from the detection system.
dependencyUncertainties.impact: A detection failure removes the cue, so the make-up action fails with it.

modelUncertainties.description: Filtration is modeled as running or failed, with no credit for degraded efficiency.
modelUncertainties.impact: Degraded filtration raises releases without failing the function, which the model does not capture.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Outside the SY success criterion and left to the radiological consequence analysis.

ccfUncertainties.description: The series isolation dampers use the air-operated valve fail-to-close factors.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Dampers of one make tested together may couple more strongly than the generic factor.

dependencyUncertainties.description: The building dampers may operate beyond their qualification in the helium and air mixture after a depressurization (SY-B14).
dependencyUncertainties.impact: A harsh environment could fail both dampers together, which the model does not yet capture.

modelUncertainties.description: The generator data count the output breaker, which is also modeled as its own event (SY-A12).
modelUncertainties.impact: Breaker closing failures are counted twice, a small conservative overlap.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Kept, since the breaker term is small against the start failure.

modelUncertainties.description: Run failures are split into the first hour and the remaining 23 hours, following the industry data.
modelUncertainties.impact: A different split would change the 24 hour generator unreliability.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Follows the structure of the industry estimates.

ccfUncertainties.description: The two generators use the diesel generator fail-to-start factors with staggered testing, since no gas-turbine data exist.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Generators in one building with one maintenance crew could couple more strongly than the industry pool.

modelUncertainties.description: Battery duty against the 24 hour mission rests on the load-shedding calculation (SY-B12).
modelUncertainties.impact: If the batteries fall short, DC is lost late in the mission, which fails protection and isolation.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Tested in the battery duty sweep.

modelUncertainties.description: The charger boundary is still open against DA (SY-A12, DA-A2).
modelUncertainties.impact: A charger fault that the output breaker fails to isolate could be counted twice or missed.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Resolve with DA before the charger estimate is final.

ccfUncertainties.description: The station batteries use the battery fail-to-operate factors across both trains.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Batteries of one make on one equalizing practice may couple more strongly.

dependencyUncertainties.description: The charger AC supply is left out on the load-shedding basis.
dependencyUncertainties.impact: If the batteries cannot carry the mission, the chargers' AC supply becomes a real dependency on the backup generators.

modelUncertainties.description: Heat exchanger fouling is treated as a failure over the mission, not as gradual degradation.
modelUncertainties.impact: A partly fouled exchanger could still remove enough heat, so the model overstates CCW failure.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Conservative.

ccfUncertainties.description: The pumps use the cooling water pump fail-to-run factors.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Pumps of one make on one maintenance schedule may couple more strongly.

modelUncertainties.description: The moisture monitor estimate comes from nonnuclear instruments whose boundary is not stated, flagged under SY-A13.
modelUncertainties.impact: Helium moisture monitors could fail more or less often than the source instruments.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distribution until vendor data exist.

ccfUncertainties.description: Both monitors use the generic demand factors, and the miscalibration error couples them too.
ccfUncertainties.impact: A shared calibration practice could defeat both monitors beyond the generic factor.

sensitivityStudies.name: SCS train count sensitivity
sensitivityStudies.description: Shutdown-cooling train count sweep across the operating states.
sensitivityStudies.results: At full power two of two trains are required, since one 7 MW train loses the decay-heat race. In the other states one of two meets the criterion with margin. Both trains catch the decay curve at 7.6 h (TF-CALC-H01).
sensitivityStudies.insights: Full power drives the two-train need, so train reliability matters most in that state.

sensitivityStudies.name: Battery duty sweep
sensitivityStudies.description: Battery duty against the mission time.
sensitivityStudies.results: Load shedding meets 24 h in the base case. The slowest case is still open under SY-B12.
sensitivityStudies.insights: The load-shedding calculation decides whether DC holds for the mission.

sensitivityStudies.name: RCCS duct coupling sweep
sensitivityStudies.description: Duct group alpha factors set to the 5th and 95th percentiles of the generic rate distribution for four-member groups (INL/EXT-21-62940 Rev. 1), with alpha 1 taking the rest.
sensitivityStudies.results: RCCS failure moves from 4.63E-3 at the 5th percentiles to 4.73E-3 at the 95th, against 4.67E-3 at the means, a change under 2 percent. The three-of-four duct term runs from 6.0E-5 to 1.7E-4.
sensitivityStudies.insights: The stack blockage and the damper misalignment dominate RCCS failure, so duct coupling is not a key source.

documentation.processDescription: Systems analysis built one system logic model at a time from the Event Sequence safety functions, with common cause groups, dependencies and human failure events placed in the models, per ASME/ANS RA-S-1.4 HLR-SY-A through C.
documentation.systemFunctionsAndBoundaries: Twelve systems modeled, each with a top event, a success criterion and a stated model boundary including the support interfaces.
documentation.systemSchematicsReferenced: System design descriptions and P&IDs referenced for each modeled system.
documentation.modeledComponentsAndFailureModes: Components and failure modes that defeat the system success criteria are included, with beneficial failures left out unless their omission distorts the result.
documentation.screeningAndExclusionJustifications: Nine components screened from detailed analysis, each against a stated screening criterion.
documentation.successCriteriaRelationship: Each system top event is set by a success criterion from Success Criteria Development.
documentation.alignmentsAndConfigurations: Normal and significant alternate alignments modeled per system.
documentation.testAndMaintenanceTreatment: Out-of-service unavailability modeled per the maintenance plan, with simultaneous planned unavailability of redundant equipment carried explicitly.
documentation.dependencySearchAndTables: Support-system dependencies set by engineering analysis in a dependency matrix, with a support-on-support loop resolved explicitly.
documentation.ccfGroupsAndModels: Twelve common cause groups, ten within a system and two across systems, consistent with the Data Analysis common cause model.
documentation.humanFailureEventsIncluded: Pre-initiator and post-initiator human failure events placed in the system models and handed to Human Reliability.
documentation.modularizationAndLogicLoops: Supercomponents stand for the protection division channels, the duct groups, the filtration trains and the generator packages, each with one recovery potential and no use by another system. No support-on-support logic loop. The backup gas-turbine generators carry their own start, cooling and lubrication equipment, so AC power needs neither Class 1E DC nor cooling water.
documentation.nomenclatureConventions: Event codes read system, component and failure mode, such as RPS-DVA-FS. Each system has one code and each failure mode one designator, so the same failure carries the same designator in every system and train and the quantifier links the trees.
documentation.digitalICTreatment: Digital protection logic modeled per the Part II Subpart 2.7 method, with software common cause modeled at CC-II.
documentation.passiveSystemsTreatment: Passive functions treated with mechanistic models and direct uncertainty propagation for functional reliability.
documentation.evaluationResultsSummary: Each system fault tree quantified standalone, with the full-plant quantification performed by Event Sequence Quantification.
documentation.informationSources: Design descriptions, failure mode analyses, the common cause parameter dossier and the surveillance plan.
documentation.modelUncertaintySources: Model uncertainty sources are recorded per system and across the plant, among them the negative temperature feedback credit, the duct coupling, the battery duty and the charger boundary.
documentation.asBuiltLimitations: Pre-operational: system models, dependencies and unavailability rest on design information pending as-built and as-operated confirmation.
documentation.praTaskInterfaces: Interfaces with Event Sequence Analysis and Success Criteria for what to model, with Data Analysis for parameters, with Human Reliability for human events, and with Event Sequence Quantification which links the trees.

comments.text: The DRACS damper group rests on a shared crew and shared make, so SY-B3 needs the grouping basis closed against the DA-D8 parameter set before the alpha factors are final.
The actuation logic carries a single software image across the trip and isolation functions, so SY-B11 needs the software common cause modeled rather than left as a bounding term.
A 4 hour battery against a 24 hour mission needs the load-shedding calculation closed under SY-B12, since the current model assumes the duty without showing it.
Two DRACS loops share the north penetration room, so SY-B8 needs the room-level dependent failure confirmed in the fault tree, not only noted in the text.
The screening of the indicating lamps and root valves is clean and each exclusion cites a stated criterion.
comments.resolution: No change required, the screening criteria are applied consistently.

variableSuccessCriteria.basis: Two of three DRACS loops remove decay heat. The full-power decay curve loses the single-loop race and two loops cross it at 4.3 h. Verified by a 41-probe dynamic campaign, capacity frontier 2.38 to 2.41 MW (TF-CALC-09).

variableSuccessCriteria.scenarioCondition: Operating states other than full power (POS-02 to POS-09)
variableSuccessCriteria.basis: One of three DRACS loops removes decay heat for the sequence mission time, since the lower decay load sits within a single loop capability.

systemConfirmationRecords.findings: Model matches the design intent, walkdown deferred to as-built.
Trip logic and divisions confirmed against the design package.
Bus assignments confirmed, battery duty flagged for INV-1.
Two-of-four voting confirmed, the software common cause carried per the digital I&C method.
Series damper arrangement and the standby clean-up train confirmed against the design package.
Lead and lag rotation confirmed, the DC room heat-up window recorded for the logic loop.
Natural-circulation path and check-valve arrangement confirmed against the coastdown analysis.
Guard-vessel retention confirmed, the bounding leak case documented.
Intermediate pump, loop isolation valve and steam-side heat sink confirmed against the design package, the steam side carried as one train.
Guard-vessel gap leak detectors and the two isolation valves confirmed against the design package.
Make-up pump, fill valve and heated tank confirmed with the designers, the operator start cued by the level alarm.
Two induction level channels and the control room alarm confirmed with the instrumentation designers.
Catch pans, drains and inert gas flooding confirmed against the fire protection design, with detection on Class 1E DC.

plantRepresentationAccuracy.basis: Models from the design package, confirmed by design review, walkdowns deferred to the as-built plant.
plantRepresentationAccuracy.sufficiencyJustification: Level of detail set to surface the risk-significant contributors against the available design information.
improvementPlans: Close the open items against Data Analysis and confirm by walkdown at as-built.

systemDependencies.details: Class 1E DC power for the trip logic.
systemDependencies.impact: Both divisions lose their trip logic.

systemDependencies.details: Trip signal from the two-of-four voting logic.
systemDependencies.impact: No trip signal reaches the rod release.

systemDependencies.details: DC power to open the air dampers.
systemDependencies.impact: The air dampers stay shut, so no loop starts natural circulation on the air side.

systemDependencies.details: Isolation signal and power for the clean-up train.
systemDependencies.impact: The dampers get no close signal and the clean-up fans stop.

systemDependencies.details: Isolation signal from the voting logic.
systemDependencies.impact: The isolation dampers get no close signal.

systemDependencies.details: Room cooling for the confinement isolation equipment.
systemDependencies.impact: None within the mission, since the dampers and accumulators need no room cooling.
systemDependencies.exclusionJustification: The isolation dampers and their air accumulators sit outside the cooled I&C rooms and need no room cooling. The voting logic that drives them carries its own room-cooling transfer.

systemDependencies.details: DC power for the voting logic and the output modules.
systemDependencies.impact: All four channels lose power, so no trip or isolation signal is generated.

systemDependencies.details: Room cooling for the safety I&C cabinets.
systemDependencies.impact: The cabinets pass their temperature limit within the mission, which fails the channels together.

systemDependencies.details: DC control power for the chillers and air handlers.
systemDependencies.impact: Both cooling trains lose their controls and stop.

systemDependencies.details: Room cooling for the battery rooms.
systemDependencies.impact: The battery rooms heat up slowly after a loss of room cooling.
systemDependencies.exclusionJustification: The battery rooms stay below their temperature limit for the 24 h mission after a loss of room cooling, per the room heat-up analysis. Leaving this direction out also breaks the loop between DC and HVAC.

systemDependencies.details: DC power for the intermediate pump.
systemDependencies.impact: The intermediate pump stops, so the loop cannot carry decay heat.

systemDependencies.details: Start signal for the intermediate loop.
systemDependencies.impact: None, since no automatic start is credited.
systemDependencies.exclusionJustification: The operator starts the intermediate loop from the control room. No automatic start signal is credited, so the voting logic is not in the start path.

systemDependencies.details: DC power for the isolation valves.
systemDependencies.impact: The isolation valves cannot close.

systemDependencies.details: Isolation signal for the leak isolation valves.
systemDependencies.impact: None, since the valves close on their own local detectors.
systemDependencies.exclusionJustification: The leak isolation valves close on their own local leak detectors, which the fault tree carries as a basic event. The voting logic is not in the isolation path.

systemDependencies.details: Falling-level alarm that cues the operator to isolate the leak.
systemDependencies.impact: The operator gets no cue, so the manual isolation backup is lost.

systemDependencies.details: DC power for the make-up pump.
systemDependencies.impact: The make-up pump cannot start.

systemDependencies.details: Falling-level alarm that cues the operator to start make-up.
systemDependencies.impact: The operator gets no cue, so make-up is not started.

systemDependencies.details: DC power for the level channels and the alarm.
systemDependencies.impact: No level signal and no alarm on a falling level.

systemDependencies.details: DC power for sodium fire detection and suppression actuation.
systemDependencies.impact: The fire is not detected and the suppression does not actuate.
