commonCauseFailureGroups.name: DRACS natural-circulation loops
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: Same make, same service conditions and same passive duty across the three loops.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: Same make, same service conditions and same passive duty across the three loops.
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: The KN gate carries the two-of-three full-power criterion, and the group carries the complete common-cause term that fails all three loops together.

commonCauseFailureGroups.name: DRACS air dampers
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: Identical dampers serviced by one crew on one procedure.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: Identical dampers serviced by one crew on one procedure.
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: The damper terms dominate the DRACS air path, carried at the air-operated valve factors.

commonCauseFailureGroups.name: RPS trip divisions
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: Two divisions of identical design and manufacture.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: Two divisions of identical design and manufacture.
defenseMechanisms: Trip channels tested on separate schedules
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: Risk significant, the divisional term sits directly under the failure-to-scram top gate.

commonCauseFailureGroups.name: Class-1E station batteries
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: Two batteries of one make sharing one room and one maintenance schedule.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: Two batteries of one make sharing one room and one maintenance schedule.
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: Risk significant, the battery term propagates through every DC-fed protective system.

commonCauseFailureGroups.name: Rod-release mechanisms
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: Identical release mechanisms on both divisions.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: Identical release mechanisms on both divisions.
defenseMechanisms: Gravity-driven insertion with no motive power
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: Carried at the generic demand factors, the release path is the last mechanical link in the trip chain.

commonCauseFailureGroups.name: Confinement isolation dampers
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: Two series dampers of one make on one test procedure.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: Two series dampers of one make on one test procedure.
defenseMechanisms: Series arrangement, either damper closes the line
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: The series pair defeats isolation only through the common term, so the group carries the path.

commonCauseFailureGroups.name: Safety chillers
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: Identical chillers in one room on one cooling-water header.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: Identical chillers in one room on one cooling-water header.
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: Room heat-up is slow, the group matters through the long I&C mission time.

commonCauseFailureGroups.name: Primary loop flow paths
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: Both loop paths share the pool and the same debris sources.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: Both loop paths share the pool and the same debris sources.
defenseMechanisms: Inlet screens on both loop suctions
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: The single shared debris source in the common pool drives the common term, carried at the generic rate factors.

commonCauseFailureGroups.name: Sensor input modules
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: Identical input modules feeding every channel.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: Identical input modules feeding every channel.
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: The sensor input events carry the module contribution through their three-of-four voting gate.

commonCauseFailureGroups.name: Output actuation modules
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: Identical output modules driving the trip and isolation loads.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: Identical output modules driving the trip and isolation loads.
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: The output actuation events carry the module contribution through their three-of-four voting gate.

commonCauseFailureGroups.name: Actuation logic software
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: One software image runs the trip and isolation voting logic.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: One software image runs the trip and isolation voting logic.
defenseMechanisms: Hardwired diverse trip path outside the image
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: An alpha factor of one on the four-channel term makes the software contribution fully dependent across all four channel events.

commonCauseFailureGroups.name: Leak isolation valves
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: Two isolation valves of one make on one test procedure.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: Two isolation valves of one make on one test procedure.
defenseMechanisms: Closure verification after each stroke test
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: The redundant pair loses isolation only through the common term, so the group carries the path.

commonCauseFailureGroups.name: Sodium level channels
commonCauseFailureGroups.description: Identical level channels feeding the alarm.
commonCauseFailureGroups.groupSelectionBasis: Identical level channels feeding the alarm.
commonCauseFailureGroups.riskSignificanceJustification: PRAXIS expands the two independent channel events into the dependent combinations during quantification.

conditionsRepresented: One cooling train lost: the other train holds the room below its limit
Both trains lost: the cabinets pass their limit within the mission, so room cooling is modeled
Loss of normal AC with the chargers off
Load shedding done within 30 minutes of the charger loss
Battery rooms without cooling for the 24 h mission
The air dampers open on DC motive power
Natural circulation needs no power once the dampers are open
Operator start from the control room
No automatic start signal credited

supportSystemSuccessCriteria.successCriteria: One battery and one bus carry the protective loads for the 24 h mission, with load shedding done within 30 minutes of a charger loss.
Two of four voting channels generate the trip or isolation signal early enough for the rods to insert within 3 s of the trip demand.
One cooling train holds the safety I&C room below its temperature limit for the 24 h mission.
One of the two level channels and the control-room alarm cue the operator on a falling sodium level.

humanFailureEventIntegrations.taskDescription: Trip setpoints miscalibrated after surveillance
humanFailureEventIntegrations.impact: Setpoints miscalibrated in both divisions delay or block the trip on demand.

humanFailureEventIntegrations.taskDescription: DRACS channels miscalibrated after surveillance
humanFailureEventIntegrations.impact: Miscalibrated channels delay the damper opening on the loops.

humanFailureEventIntegrations.taskDescription: Dampers left misaligned after surveillance
humanFailureEventIntegrations.impact: Dampers left misaligned cut the air flow through the affected loops.

humanFailureEventIntegrations.taskDescription: Pump trip circuits miscalibrated after surveillance
humanFailureEventIntegrations.impact: Miscalibrated trip circuits delay the pump trip and the start of natural circulation.

humanFailureEventIntegrations.taskDescription: Operator fails to start the standby clean-up train
humanFailureEventIntegrations.impact: No clean-up flow after the running train stops.

humanFailureEventIntegrations.taskDescription: Charger left in the wrong mode after maintenance
humanFailureEventIntegrations.impact: Charger A left in the wrong mode, so bank A discharges instead of floating.

humanFailureEventIntegrations.taskDescription: Both battery banks held off float after equalization
humanFailureEventIntegrations.impact: Both banks stay off float after the joint equalization, so neither can carry its bus on a charger loss.

humanFailureEventIntegrations.taskDescription: Operator fails to start backup decay heat removal
humanFailureEventIntegrations.impact: Backup decay heat removal stays off when the intermediate loop is lost.

humanFailureEventIntegrations.taskDescription: Operator fails to isolate the leak path
humanFailureEventIntegrations.impact: The leak path stays open, so the pool level keeps falling.

humanFailureEventIntegrations.taskDescription: Operator fails to initiate make-up
humanFailureEventIntegrations.impact: No make-up flow, so the pool level keeps falling.

humanFailureEventIntegrations.taskDescription: Operator fails to respond to the fire alarm
humanFailureEventIntegrations.impact: The fire grows past the cell before the operators respond.

isolationTripConditions.condition: Primary pump trip on the reactor trip signal, which starts natural circulation.
Clean-up fan trip on high filter differential pressure, counted in the running fan fails-to-run data.
Battery output breaker trip on a downstream bus fault, counted in the battery train fails-to-run data.
Chiller trip on high condenser pressure, counted in the cooling train fails-to-run data.
Intermediate loop isolation on a sodium-water reaction signal in the steam generator.
Make-up pump trip on low tank level.
isolationTripConditions.exclusionJustification: The tank holds more than the design make-up volume, so the trip cannot actuate within the mission time.

modularizationRecords.justification: Neither part of a division can be recovered once the trip demand passes, and no other system draws on the division logic. The breakers and rods stay apart because they fail in different ways.

representedComponentIds: Loop piping and sodium-to-air heat exchanger
modularizationRecords.justification: A loop cannot be recovered once natural circulation fails, and no other system uses the loops. The air dampers and air paths stay apart because they fail in different ways and carry their own data.
The steam side is restored as one train, and no other modeled system draws on it. The intermediate pump and the isolation valve stay apart because the sodium side has its own data.
The suppression acts once and cannot be recovered after the fire spreads, and no other system uses it.

simultaneousUnavailabilityEvents.description: Filter change on the clean-up train
simultaneousUnavailabilityEvents.plannedActivityBasis: The filter change isolates the clean-up train at damper A, so both are out for the change. Pre-operational assumption from the design maintenance plan, about 18 hours a year at power.

simultaneousUnavailabilityEvents.description: Joint equalizing charge of both battery banks
simultaneousUnavailabilityEvents.plannedActivityBasis: The design test plan equalizes both banks in one evolution once a year. The chargers carry the buses meanwhile, so both batteries are unavailable for about 22 hours.

componentScreeningJustifications.quantitativeJustification: 3.9E-6 over 24 h from the industry-average air-operated damper spurious operation rate (AOD-SOP) of 1.61E-7 per hour, against 6.9E-3 for loop 1 failing to maintain natural circulation. The ratio is 1,790, above 100.

componentScreeningJustifications.componentId: Train A chiller bypass valve opens spuriously
componentScreeningJustifications.quantitativeJustification: 6.1E-7 over 24 h from the industry-average motor-operated valve spurious operation rate (MOV-SOP) of 2.54E-8 per hour, against 9.3E-4 for cooling train A failing to run. The ratio is 1,530, above 100.

componentScreeningJustifications.componentId: Intermediate loop dump valve opens spuriously
componentScreeningJustifications.quantitativeJustification: 6.1E-7 over 24 h from the industry-average motor-operated valve spurious operation rate (MOV-SOP) of 2.54E-8 per hour, against 6.2E-4 for the intermediate sodium pump failing to run. The ratio is 1,020, above 100.

componentScreeningJustifications.componentId: Isolation valve A small external leakage
componentScreeningJustifications.quantitativeJustification: 1.4E-6 over 72 h from the industry-average motor-operated valve small external leakage rate (MOV-ELS) of 1.88E-8 per hour, against 2.3E-4 for valve A failing to close. That is 0.59 percent of the component's failures, under 1 percent, and both leave the leak path open.

componentScreeningJustifications.componentId: Recirculation line manual valve transfers open
componentScreeningJustifications.quantitativeJustification: 1.4E-6 over 72 h from the industry-average manual valve spurious operation rate (XVM-SOP) of 1.88E-8 per hour, against 1.2E-3 for the make-up pump failing to start. The ratio is 868, above 100.

environmentalDesignBasisConsiderations.environmentalConditions: North penetration room. A fire or flood here fails two of the three DRACS loops at once, carried through the environment factor of the loop common cause group.
Shared safety HVAC. A loss of room cooling heats the safety I&C cabinets in all four channels together, carried as the room-cooling transfer in the actuation fault tree.
Sodium-fire environment. A sodium leak can push the isolation dampers beyond their environmental qualification, so the adverse condition enters as a dependent failure.

initiationActuationSystems.name: Reactor trip actuation
initiationActuationSystems.description: Flux, flow and temperature channels vote two of four in the actuation logic, which releases the rods.
initiationActuationSystems.softwareModelingApproach: Common software image modeled as CCF-ACT-SW across the four channels.

initiationActuationSystems.name: Confinement isolation actuation
initiationActuationSystems.description: The voting logic closes the series isolation dampers on high activity or a sodium-fire signal.
initiationActuationSystems.softwareModelingApproach: Same software image as the trip, in CCF-ACT-SW.

initiationActuationSystems.name: Backup decay heat removal start
initiationActuationSystems.description: The operator starts the intermediate loop from the control room.
initiationActuationSystems.softwareModelingApproach: No software in the start path.

initiationActuationSystems.name: Leak isolation actuation
initiationActuationSystems.description: Local leak detectors close the isolation valves, with an operator backup cued by the level alarm.
initiationActuationSystems.softwareModelingApproach: No software in the isolation path.

digitalInstrumentationAndControl.name: Trip and isolation voting logic
digitalInstrumentationAndControl.description: Digital voting logic for the trip and isolation functions.
digitalInstrumentationAndControl.methodology: Channel-level sensor, output and software events voted two of four, with the common software image in CCF-ACT-SW.
specialConsiderations: Software common cause modeled through CCF-ACT-SW at CC-II.

passiveSystemsTreatments.name: DRACS natural circulation
passiveSystemsTreatments.description: Decay heat removed by buoyancy-driven natural circulation, no active power.
passiveSystemsTreatments.uncertaintyEvaluation: Reliability propagated by direct uncertainty quantification.

passiveSystemsTreatments.name: Primary loop natural circulation
passiveSystemsTreatments.description: Buoyancy-driven flow establishes on a pump trip.
passiveSystemsTreatments.uncertaintyEvaluation: Establishment timing carried as the sensitive variable.

passiveSystemsTreatments.name: Guard vessel
passiveSystemsTreatments.description: Passive structural barrier that bounds a primary leak.

depletionModels.basis: Lasts 4 h at the full protective load. Load shedding within 30 minutes extends the duty to the 24 h mission, and that calculation is under review.

depletionModels.description: Instrument air accumulators for the isolation dampers
depletionModels.basis: The accumulators hold the dampers closed for 72 h, three times the 24 h mission.
The atmosphere is the heat sink, so there is no inventory to run out.

potentialExceedanceScenarios: Decay heat above the rated exchanger duty early in the sequence
overCapacityConsiderations.justificationForCapability: Rated capability used at CC-I until the realistic duty is confirmed.

potentialExceedanceScenarios: Natural-circulation flow near the loop capability
overCapacityConsiderations.justificationForCapability: Realistic capability supported by the coastdown analysis at CC-II.

potentialExceedanceScenarios: Sodium spill loads at the bounding leak size
overCapacityConsiderations.justificationForCapability: Design-basis structural capability used until the spill analysis is extended.

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: Three loops, each with its loop, air damper and air path, with loop surveillance, the loop and damper common cause and the channel and damper errors. Class 1E DC enters by transfer.
techniques: Compared with the DRACS design description
Checked the two-of-three full-power criterion against the model logic
modelValidations.results: Loop-level detail matches the sodium test facility data and carries the variable success criteria.

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: Each division modeled as its trip logic, scram breaker and rod latch, with the division and rod common cause and the setpoint miscalibration. Actuation logic and Class 1E DC enter by transfer.
techniques: Compared with the protection system design description
Checked each division event against its DA boundary
modelValidations.results: Division-level detail surfaces the contributors that matter, the division and rod common cause and the miscalibration.

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: Four voting channels, each with its sensor input, output module and software, voted two of four, with common cause for each module type and for the software.
techniques: Compared with the digital I&C design description
Applied the digital I&C method at CC-II
modelValidations.results: Module-level detail meets the CC-II software requirement, with the software boundary flagged under SY-A13.

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: Two battery trains, each with its battery, charger and DC bus, with the battery common cause, the equalizing outages and the charger and float errors.
techniques: Compared with the electrical power design information
Checked the charger and battery boundaries against DA
modelValidations.results: Train-level detail matches the data except at the charger-to-battery interface.
issuesIdentified: Charger-to-battery boundary still under reconciliation with DA (DA-A2)

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: Two isolation dampers, the running and standby clean-up fans, and the inlet valve and inlet damper, with the damper common cause, the joint filter change and the operator start. Actuation and Class 1E DC enter by transfer.
techniques: Compared with the confinement design information
Checked the joint outage against the DA coincident maintenance record
modelValidations.results: Damper, fan and valve detail matches the data.

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: Two cooling trains, each with its chiller and air handler, with the train common cause and the temperature channel that starts the standby train. Class 1E DC enters by transfer.
techniques: Compared with the room cooling design information
modelValidations.results: Component-level detail matches the data.

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: Two loop flow paths and check valves and the thermal center, with the flow common cause and the pump trip miscalibration.
techniques: Compared with the coastdown and natural-circulation analysis
modelValidations.results: Loop-level detail matches the natural-circulation analysis.

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: A system-level model from the structural analysis. The guard vessel is a passive barrier with no active parts.
techniques: Compared with the structural analysis of the bounding leak
modelValidations.results: A system-level model is enough because failure is set by the structural retention itself.

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: The intermediate pump, the steam-side heat sink and the loop isolation valve, with pump maintenance and the operator start. Class 1E DC enters by transfer.
techniques: Compared with the intermediate loop design information
modelValidations.results: Component-level detail on the sodium side. The steam side stays one event because it is a backup path, with its boundary flagged under SY-A13.

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: The leak detection channel and two isolation valves, with the valve common cause and the operator isolation. Class 1E DC and the level alarm enter by transfer.
techniques: Compared with the leak detection and isolation design information
modelValidations.results: Valve-level detail matches the data, with the leak detectors flagged under SY-A13.

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: The make-up pump, fill valve and tank, with the operator start. Class 1E DC and the level alarm enter by transfer.
techniques: Compared with the make-up design information
modelValidations.results: Component-level detail matches the data, with the pump boundary flagged under SY-A13.

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: Two level channels and the alarm, with the channel common cause. Class 1E DC enters by transfer.
techniques: Compared with the level instrumentation design information
modelValidations.results: Channel-level detail matches the design, with the probe boundary flagged under SY-A13.

modelValidations.name: Level of detail
modelValidations.description: The fire detection and the suppression and drain, with the operator response. Class 1E DC enters by transfer.
techniques: Compared with the fire protection design
modelValidations.results: Function-level detail is enough for a single-train system, with both boundaries flagged under SY-A13.

componentBoundaryReviews.note: The rod data come from pressurized-water reactor rods. The latch release is outside that population, so the boundary cannot be checked until design-specific data exist.
Software has no industry data boundary. The estimate follows the digital I&C method, so the fit is flagged until platform data are in hand.

The charger event covers a charger fault that the output breaker fails to isolate from the bank. DA still has the charger-to-battery interface under reconciliation (DA-A2), so the boundary stays open until both sides agree.
The pump data come from water service. The sodium pump cooling and seals are outside that population, so the fit is flagged until vendor data are in hand.
No industry boundary covers a whole steam-side train. Flagged until the train is split into components or plant data exist.
Sodium leak detectors have no industry data boundary. Flagged until vendor data are in hand.
The pump data come from water service. The sodium pump cooling and seals are outside that population, so the fit is flagged until vendor data are in hand.
Induction level probes in sodium are outside the industry sensor records. Flagged until vendor data are in hand.
Sodium fire detectors have no industry data boundary. Flagged until vendor data are in hand.
No industry component matches a sodium fire suppression system. Flagged until test data for the catch pans and flooding are in hand.

nomenclatureDesignators.meaning: Fails on demand to start, trip or operate
Out of service for test or maintenance

modelUncertainties.description: No credit is taken for inherent reactivity feedback on a failure to insert the rods.
modelUncertainties.impact: Metal fuel feedback could limit power without a trip, so the model overstates the failure-to-trip consequences.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Conservative and consistent with the SC criterion.

modelUncertainties.description: Rod release uses pressurized-water reactor rod data, flagged under SY-A13.
modelUncertainties.impact: Latched rods released by opening a holding circuit could fail more or less often than the industry drives.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distribution until design-specific data exist.

ccfUncertainties.description: The division group uses the generic demand factors for the trip logic, with staggered testing.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Divisions of one design could couple more strongly after a common maintenance error.

ccfUncertainties.description: The rod release group uses the generic demand factors, since no rod latch template exists.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Latches of one design in one sodium environment may couple more strongly.

dependencyUncertainties.description: Both divisions take their trip signal from the shared actuation logic through one transfer.
dependencyUncertainties.impact: The division redundancy does not extend to the actuation logic, so its common cause sets a floor on RPS failure.

modelUncertainties.description: Two of three loops are needed at full power, from the dynamic campaign (TF-CALC-09).
modelUncertainties.impact: A one-of-three criterion would cut the two-of-three loop term, a small part of DRACS failure.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Criterion from SC. The damper misalignment, DC and the channel miscalibration dominate DRACS failure.

modelUncertainties.description: Loop natural circulation failures come from sodium test facility experience.
modelUncertainties.impact: A small facility population gives a wide loop estimate.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distribution.

ccfUncertainties.description: Loop factors come from the generic rate data for three-member groups, passed as staggered MGL values.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Coupling between the passive loops sets the two-of-three loop term.

ccfUncertainties.description: The damper grouping basis and its air-operated valve factors are open against DA-D8 (SY-B3, B4).
ccfUncertainties.impact: Stronger damper coupling would fail two or more loops at once.

dependencyUncertainties.description: Two DRACS loops share the north penetration room, and the fault tree update is open (SY-B8).
dependencyUncertainties.impact: A room hazard could fail two loops together and defeat the two-of-three criterion.

dependencyUncertainties.description: The dampers need Class 1E DC to open, carried as one transfer for all three loops.
dependencyUncertainties.impact: Loss of DC fails every loop, so the DC failure probability adds directly to DRACS failure.

modelUncertainties.description: Natural circulation is credited from the coastdown analysis, with the thermal-center margin as the sensitive variable.
modelUncertainties.impact: A smaller elevation margin would slow or prevent natural circulation.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Margin uncertainty is propagated in the passive system analysis (PST-PCS).

ccfUncertainties.description: Blockage of both flow paths uses the generic rate factors.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Debris in the pool couples the loops. One shared debris source may couple them more strongly than the generic rate pool.

modelUncertainties.description: Clean-up filtration is modeled as running or failed, with no credit for degraded efficiency.
modelUncertainties.impact: Degraded filtration raises releases without failing the function, which the model does not capture.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Outside the SY success criterion and left to the radiological consequence analysis.

ccfUncertainties.description: The series isolation dampers use the air-operated valve fail-to-close factors.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Dampers of one make tested together may couple more strongly than the generic factor.

dependencyUncertainties.description: Confinement dampers in the sodium-fire environment may operate beyond their qualification (SY-B14).
dependencyUncertainties.impact: A sodium fire could fail both dampers together, which the model does not yet capture.

modelUncertainties.description: The guard vessel is modeled at the system level from the structural analysis of the bounding leak.
modelUncertainties.impact: A leak larger than the bounding case or a weld flaw could defeat retention.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: System-level reliability from the structural analysis, not sampled in a fault tree.

modelUncertainties.description: Battery duty against the 24 hour mission rests on the load-shedding calculation (SY-B12).
modelUncertainties.impact: If the batteries fall short, DC is lost late in the mission, which fails the trip logic, the dampers and the actuation.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Tested in the battery duty sweep.

modelUncertainties.description: The charger boundary is still open against DA (SY-A12, DA-A2).
modelUncertainties.impact: A charger fault that the output breaker fails to isolate could be counted twice or missed.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Resolve with DA before the charger estimate is final.

ccfUncertainties.description: The station batteries use the battery fail-to-operate factors across both trains.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Batteries of one make on one equalizing practice may couple more strongly.

dependencyUncertainties.description: Battery room cooling is left out on the room heat-up calculation, which breaks the DC and HVAC loop.
dependencyUncertainties.impact: If the room heats faster than calculated, battery capacity drops within the mission.

modelUncertainties.description: Software failure is estimated per the digital I&C method at 1.5E-4 per demand per channel, from expert elicitation EJ-04, flagged under SY-A13.
modelUncertainties.impact: No industry data stand behind the software estimate, so its error factor of 7.2 may understate the spread.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distribution, with the software common cause in its own group.

ccfUncertainties.description: Software common cause is modeled as all four channels failing together, with the CC-II software model open (SY-B11).
ccfUncertainties.impact: The software group sets the floor on actuation failure.

ccfUncertainties.description: Sensor input modules use the generic rate alpha factors for four-member groups.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Modules of one platform may couple more strongly than the industry pool.

ccfUncertainties.description: Output modules use the generic demand alpha factors for four-member groups.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Modules of one platform may couple more strongly than the industry pool.

dependencyUncertainties.description: The I&C cabinets need room cooling, carried as a transfer to HVAC.
dependencyUncertainties.impact: If the cabinets tolerate a higher temperature than assumed, the HVAC transfer overstates actuation failure.

modelUncertainties.description: The room heat-up time without cooling comes from the design heat load, with no credit for opening doors.
modelUncertainties.impact: Operators could slow the heat-up, so the model overstates the effect of losing room cooling.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Conservative.

ccfUncertainties.description: The chillers use the generic rate factors.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Chillers of one make in one room may couple more strongly than the generic factor.

modelUncertainties.description: The steam-side heat sink is one train-level event, flagged under SY-A13.
modelUncertainties.impact: Failures inside the steam train and their support needs are not separated.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Split the train into components when the design matures.

modelUncertainties.description: The intermediate pump uses water-service pump data, flagged under SY-A13.
modelUncertainties.impact: Sodium pump cooling and seals are outside that population.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distribution until vendor data exist.

modelUncertainties.description: Sodium leak detectors in the guard-vessel gap have no industry data, flagged under SY-A13.
modelUncertainties.impact: The detectors could fail more or less often than the generic estimate.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distribution until vendor data exist.

ccfUncertainties.description: The isolation valve pair uses the motor-operated valve fail-to-close factors.
ccfUncertainties.impact: Valves of one make on one stroke-test schedule may couple more strongly than the generic factor.

dependencyUncertainties.description: The operator's cue to isolate comes from the level alarm in the detection system.
dependencyUncertainties.impact: A detection failure removes the cue, so the operator backup is not independent.

modelUncertainties.description: The make-up tank is modeled as available or unavailable, with the trace heaters inside its boundary.
modelUncertainties.impact: A partly frozen tank could still deliver some sodium, so the model overstates make-up failure.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Conservative.

modelUncertainties.description: The make-up pump uses water-service pump data, flagged under SY-A13.
modelUncertainties.impact: Sodium pump cooling and seals are outside that population.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distribution until vendor data exist.

dependencyUncertainties.description: The operator starts make-up on the level alarm from the detection system.
dependencyUncertainties.impact: A detection failure removes the cue, so the make-up action fails with it.

modelUncertainties.description: Induction level probes in sodium have no industry data, flagged under SY-A13.
modelUncertainties.impact: The probes could fail more or less often than the generic estimate.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distribution until vendor data exist.

ccfUncertainties.description: The two level channels use the generic demand factors and share one calibration practice.
ccfUncertainties.impact: A shared calibration error couples the channels beyond the generic factor.

modelUncertainties.description: Sodium fire detection and suppression have no industry data, flagged under SY-A13.
modelUncertainties.impact: The estimates could be far from the real performance of the catch pans and the inert gas flooding.
modelUncertainties.treatmentApproach: Carried through the DA distributions until test data exist.

sensitivityStudies.name: DRACS loop coupling sweep
sensitivityStudies.description: Three-loop alpha 3 set to the 5th and 95th percentiles of the generic rate distribution (INL/EXT-21-62940 Rev. 1), with alpha 2 at its mean and alpha 1 taking the rest, passed as staggered MGL values.
sensitivityStudies.results: DRACS failure moves from 1.740E-2 to 1.745E-2, against 1.742E-2 at the means, a change under half a percent. The two-of-three loop term runs from 5.63E-4 to 6.12E-4.
sensitivityStudies.insights: The damper misalignment, DC and the channel miscalibration dominate DRACS failure, so loop coupling is not a key source.

sensitivityStudies.name: Battery duty sweep
sensitivityStudies.description: Battery duty against the mission time.
sensitivityStudies.results: Load shedding meets 24 h in the base case. The slowest case is still open under SY-B12.
sensitivityStudies.insights: The load-shedding calculation decides whether DC holds for the mission.

uncertaintySources.source: Industry component data from light-water reactors applied to sodium-service pumps, valves and instruments
uncertaintySources.impact: These estimates may not reflect sodium service, which shifts the heat removal, isolation, make-up and detection results.

uncertaintySources.source: Generic common cause factors from light-water reactor experience
uncertaintySources.impact: Coupling in sodium-service and passive groups may differ, which shifts every redundant system.

uncertaintySources.source: Design information in place of the as-built plant
uncertaintySources.impact: Models, boundaries and support needs may change at the as-built confirmation (SY-A6).

relatedAssumptions.assumption: No repair of failed equipment is credited within the mission time (SY-A31).
relatedAssumptions.basis: No plant repair data exist before operation.

relatedAssumptions.assumption: Each support system enters a fault tree through one transfer to its top event.
relatedAssumptions.basis: Train assignments of the support buses are not final in the design package.

relatedAssumptions.assumption: Mission times come from the SC workbook for each sequence family, with 72 hours for the guard vessel.
relatedAssumptions.basis: SC mission times per sequence family.

reasonableAlternatives.alternative: Technology-specific data from sodium facilities for all sodium-service components
reasonableAlternatives.reasonNotSelected: The facility records cover only the DRACS loops, air paths, flow paths and thermal center, so the other sodium components use industry data.

reasonableAlternatives.alternative: Train-level transfers to the support systems
reasonableAlternatives.reasonNotSelected: The bus and train assignments are not final, so system-level transfers stand until the as-built single-line diagrams exist.

documentation.processDescription: Systems analysis built one system logic model at a time from the Event Sequence safety functions, with common cause groups, dependencies and human failure events placed in the models, per ASME/ANS RA-S-1.4 HLR-SY-A through C.
documentation.systemFunctionsAndBoundaries: Eight systems modeled, each with a top event, a success criterion and a stated model boundary including the support interfaces.
documentation.systemSchematicsReferenced: System design descriptions and P&IDs referenced for each modeled system.
documentation.modeledComponentsAndFailureModes: Components and failure modes that defeat the system success criteria are included, with beneficial failures left out unless their omission distorts the result.
documentation.screeningAndExclusionJustifications: Five components screened from detailed analysis, each against a stated screening criterion.
documentation.successCriteriaRelationship: Each system top event is set by a success criterion from Success Criteria Development.
documentation.alignmentsAndConfigurations: Normal and significant alternate alignments modeled per system.
documentation.testAndMaintenanceTreatment: Out-of-service unavailability modeled per the maintenance plan, with simultaneous planned unavailability of redundant equipment carried explicitly.
documentation.dependencySearchAndTables: Support-system dependencies set by engineering analysis in a dependency matrix, with a support-on-support loop resolved explicitly.
documentation.ccfGroupsAndModels: Thirteen common cause groups, nine within a system and four across systems, consistent with the Data Analysis common cause model.
documentation.humanFailureEventsIncluded: Pre-initiator and post-initiator human failure events placed in the system models and handed to Human Reliability.
documentation.modularizationAndLogicLoops: Supercomponents stand for the protection division channels, the DRACS loops, the steam-side heat sink and the fire suppression, each with one recovery potential and no use by another system. One support-on-support logic loop resolved by crediting the battery for the cooling restart window.
documentation.nomenclatureConventions: Event codes read system, component and failure mode, such as RPS-DVA-FS. Each system has one code and each failure mode one designator, so the same failure carries the same designator in every system and train and the quantifier links the trees.
documentation.digitalICTreatment: Digital actuation logic modeled per the Part II Subpart 2.7 method, with software common cause modeled at CC-II.
documentation.passiveSystemsTreatment: Passive functions treated with mechanistic models and direct uncertainty propagation for functional reliability.
documentation.evaluationResultsSummary: Each system fault tree quantified standalone, with the full-plant quantification performed by Event Sequence Quantification.
documentation.informationSources: Design descriptions, failure mode analyses, the common cause parameter dossier and the surveillance plan.
documentation.modelUncertaintySources: Model uncertainty sources are recorded per system and across the plant, among them the feedback credit, the loop and damper coupling, the battery duty and the actuation software.
documentation.asBuiltLimitations: Pre-operational: system models, dependencies and unavailability rest on design information pending as-built and as-operated confirmation.
documentation.praTaskInterfaces: Interfaces with Event Sequence Analysis and Success Criteria for what to model, with Data Analysis for parameters, with Human Reliability for human events, and with Event Sequence Quantification which links the trees.

sources.name: WSRC-TR-93-262 Rev. 1, Savannah River Site generic data base (1998)
sources.covers: Recommended lognormal failure rates for about 500 water, chemical process, compressed gas, HVAC, electrical and instrument component modes, with the category 1, 2 and 3 source data and aggregated results behind them
sources.boundaryConvention: Components and failure modes follow a Savannah River Site list in six system types: water, chemical process, compressed gas, HVAC/exhaust, electrical distribution, and instrumentation and control. Each row has an identifier made of a component code, a failure mode code and a system code (Tables 7 to 9), such as PIP-LE-W for external leakage of water piping. Pipe, hose, tube and duct rates are per hour per foot and the cable rate is per 1000 ft. Leak and rupture values taken from EGG-SSRE-9639 define rupture as a leak of more than 50 gpm.
sources.failureCounting: Category 1 sources give failure counts with reviewed populations and exposures, from nuclear power plant PRAs and Swedish plant data gathered in NUCLARR, plus Savannah River Site reactor data. Category 2 sources give actual failure data with added uncertainty, such as LER and in-plant reliability surveys of nuclear plant components, NPRD-3, OREDA, the Idaho Chemical Processing Plant (WIN-330), a tritium handling facility and an LNG plant. Category 3 sources list only failure rate estimates, from WASH-1400, the CCPS guidelines, IEEE Std 500-1984, a natural gas facility study, two EPRI power plant reports and EGG-SSRE-8875. Counts are failures over component hours or demands, and judgment was used to split failures among failure modes.
sources.quality: Within a category, data sets were pooled by matching the moments of a lognormal distribution, and sparse data used a Bayesian update of a noninformative prior with an error factor of 10. Category 3 estimates were combined by averaging lognormal parameters. The recommended value takes category 1 first, then category 2, then category 3, rounded to 1, 3 or 5 times a power of 10, and Rev. 1 limits error factors to 10. The data years are not printed, so 1998, the Rev. 1 date, bounds them. The report is a scan, so every value was read from the page images.
sources.reference: A. Blanchard and B. N. Roy, Savannah River Site Generic Data Base Development, WSRC-TR-93-262 Rev. 1 (WSMSC-98-0162), Westinghouse Savannah River Company and Westinghouse Safety Management Solutions, May 1998 (original issue 1993)

sources.covers: Operating history of the five helium circulators at Fort St. Vrain, the only U.S. high-temperature gas-cooled power reactor, through 1987.
sources.boundaryConvention: The circulator machine: axial helium compressor, steam turbine drive, water turbine backup drive, shaft seals and water-lubricated bearings. The paper keeps problems of the bearing water and buffer helium auxiliaries apart.
sources.failureCounting: An incident is any event that needed one or more circulators removed for repair. Each is classed as a design or manufacturing defect, a random failure, or external or other. The paper counts fourteen incidents, eleven defects, one random failure and three external problems, over about 250,000 combined machine hours.
sources.quality: One plant, one design and five machines. The source calls the classification tentative. Several defects were corrected early, so the count is pessimistic for later service.

sources.name: NaSCoRD sodium component reliability database
sources.covers: Sodium pump, valve and filter failure rates with their priors
sources.boundaryConvention: Components as recorded in the CREDO engineering data. Valves are grouped by actuator type, pumps as mechanical or electromagnetic, and filters by unit. Failure modes follow the EG&G Idaho categories.
sources.failureCounting: Failures come from CREDO event records and unusual occurrence reports, cleaned by the SNL and EG&G Idaho recommendations. Operating hours come from reactor state records. Demand counts are not reliable yet, so the source advises against per-demand rates.
sources.quality: Thousands of components and millions of operating hours from EBR-II, FFTF and U.S. sodium test loops. Pump and valve rates are Bayesian posteriors on the EG&G Idaho prior. Filter rates are failures over hours. Japanese data held in CREDO are not in NaSCoRD.
sources.reference: Denman, Stuart and Jankovsky, SAND2017-9517, Sandia National Laboratories, 2017, with the sodium valve paper (PSAM 14, 2018), the sodium pump paper (2019) and the sodium filter paper (2021)

sources.name: CCF Parameter Estimations, 2020 Update, Revision 1 (INL/EXT-21-62940)
sources.covers: Alpha factor distributions, MLEs and MGL parameters for CCCG sizes 2 to 8 by component, system and failure mode, plus generic and prior distributions
sources.boundaryConvention: Each CCF template is a query rule over the NRC CCF database by component type, failure mode and, where named, system or plant group. Pooled templates cover all systems. A CCF event needs two or more failed or degraded components at one plant and in one system, from a single shared cause. Failures caused by equipment outside the component boundary are excluded.
sources.failureCounting: CCF events and independent failure counts come from the NRC CCF database for 1/1/2006 to 12/31/2020, queried in RADS with the SPAR Rules 2020 folder. Each event is coded as an impact vector with degradation, timing and shared cause factors and mapped to CCCG sizes 2 to 8. Only CCF events are counted and unavailability events are excluded.
sources.quality: Each template is a Bayesian update of the 2015 generic Dirichlet prior (1997-2015 data) with the mapped impact vectors. The report prints the 5th, mean, median and 95th values, the MLE and the Beta marginal a and b, and converts mean alpha factors to MGL parameters. Many system-specific templates have zero CCF events and stay close to the prior. Two templates (ALL-PDP-FR and CCF-DEM) print summary tables that do not match their distribution tables.
sources.reference: Z. Ma and K. J. Kvarfordt, CCF Parameter Estimations, 2020 Update, INL/EXT-21-62940 Revision 1, Idaho National Laboratory, August 2022

sources.name: SAND2022-14164 Compressed Natural Gas Component Leak Frequency Estimation
sources.covers: Annual leak frequency distributions for 11 CNG component types in five leak area bins, plus the literature leak frequencies behind them
sources.boundaryConvention: Components are binned by type only: compressor, filter, flange or gasket, heat exchanger, hose, instrument, joint, jumper, pipe, valve and vessel. Sizes and subtypes are pooled, so one valve estimate covers every valve. Leak size is the leak area as a fraction of the flow area of the connected piping, in bins of 0.01%, 0.1%, 1%, 10% and 100%.
sources.failureCounting: No events are counted. The inputs are published leak frequencies from a literature review, listed in Appendix A and mapped to leak area bins by qualitative labels or by area ratios. Only compressed gas data feed the model when they exist, and instruments and joints use generic data. The years shown are the publication years of the data sources.
sources.quality: A Bayesian log-linear model of log frequency against log leak area is fit by Markov chain Monte Carlo for each component. The compressed gas data are sparse and old, and none fall in the 0.01% and 0.1% bins, so those bins are extrapolated. The authors warn that the uncertainty may be underestimated and recommend the medians for QRA.
sources.reference: D. Brooks, A. Glover, B. D. Ehrhart, SAND2022-14164, Sandia National Laboratories, October 2022

sources.name: SAND2020-10828 Hydrogen Plant Hazards and Risk Analysis for Siting near Nuclear Power Plants
sources.covers: Generic and hydrogen component leak frequencies by leak size, facility leak frequency for a steam electrolysis hydrogen plant, and wind fragilities of nuclear plant structures and switchyard parts
sources.boundaryConvention: Leak frequencies are per component type with subtypes and sizes pooled. Leak size is the leak area as a fraction of the total flow area: very small 0.01%, minor 0.1%, medium 1%, major 10% and rupture 100%. Pipe frequencies are per meter of pipe. Fragilities are conditional failure probabilities of plant structures and switchyard parts at a given wind speed.
sources.failureCounting: Generic leak frequencies are published values from chemical process, compressed gas, nuclear and offshore sources (Table B-1), published from 1975 to 2007. Hydrogen leak counts over component-years come from Compressed Gas Association members through NFPA 2 TG6, cited from LaChance et al. (SAND2009-0874), and are not shown. Wind fragilities are taken from the Duane Arnold IPEEE and a Vogtle high wind study.
sources.quality: A Bayesian log-linear model of leak frequency against leak area is fit by Markov chain Monte Carlo to the generic data and then updated with the hydrogen counts. Generic data exist only for the 1%, 10% and 100% bins, so smaller bins are extrapolated. The facility frequency multiplies assumed component counts and pipe lengths for a postulated design.
sources.reference: A. Glover, A. Baird, D. Brooks, SAND2020-10828, Sandia National Laboratories, October 2020

sources.name: NUREG-1829, Estimating Loss-of-Coolant Accident (LOCA) Frequencies Through the Elicitation Process, Vols. 1 and 2
sources.covers: Expert elicitation LOCA frequencies for BWRs and PWRs by flow rate category and plant age, with sensitivity cases, plus base case pipe failure rates, LOCA frequencies and PFM probabilities.
sources.boundaryConvention: LOCA categories are cumulative flow rate thresholds from more than 100 gpm to more than 500,000 gpm, each with a BWR and a PWR effective break size. Only passive primary pressure boundary failures count, both piping and non-piping such as the vessel, nozzles, valve bodies, pump casings and steam generator tubes. Active failures such as stuck-open valves and pump seal LOCAs are excluded. Panelists used ASME rules to split piping from non-piping.
sources.failureCounting: No LOCA of Category 2 or larger has occurred, so the estimates rest on expert judgment anchored to base cases. The base cases use pipe failure records from about 1970 to 2003 (PIPExp, SLAP and LERs) and PFM codes. Category 1 checks use U.S. operating experience to December 2006. Frequencies are per calendar year unless a table states reactor years.
sources.quality: Twelve panelists gave median and 5th and 95th percentile ratios relative to the base cases. Responses were combined as split lognormals and aggregated with the geometric mean, with arithmetic-mean and mixture aggregation as sensitivity cases. Uncertainty is very large and the group results depend most on the aggregation method. The report does not recommend one set of estimates for all uses.
sources.reference: R. Tregoning, L. Abramson, P. Scott, NUREG-1829 Vols. 1 and 2, U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, April 2008

sources.name: NUREG-1715 Component Performance Study, Vols. 1-4 (turbine-driven pumps, motor-driven pumps, air-operated valves, motor-operated valves)
sources.covers: Probability of failure on demand, standby failure rates, failures per component-year and failure cause shares for safety-related pumps and valves in U.S. light water reactors
sources.boundaryConvention: A turbine-driven pump assembly is the pump, turbine driver and governor with their piece parts. Steam inlet, suction and discharge valves, flow instruments and remote controls are outside. A motor-driven pump assembly is the pump, motor and circuit breaker. Valve assemblies are the valve body plus the air or motor operator, without MSIVs, PORVs, non-integral instrument air parts or the MOV circuit breaker.
sources.failureCounting: Only complete failures of Application Coded components in risk-important systems count. NPRDS gives surveillance test failures and test frequencies for 1987-1995, and LERs in SCSS give ESF actuation failures and demands for 1987-1998. Pump start and run failures and valve open, close and operate failures are pooled as failure on demand. Surveillance demands are estimated from test frequency, component count and years.
sources.quality: Failure on demand uses a Bayes method with a beta plant-to-plant distribution fit by maximum likelihood, or a noninformative prior for sparse data, with 90% intervals. Classical 90% chi-square intervals are given for information. Standby rates divide failures by calendar component-hours, so they are not run-time rates. The volumes are scanned and some printed values disagree between tables, which the affected entries note.
sources.reference: J. R. Houghton and H. G. Hamzehee (Vols. 1-2) and J. R. Houghton (Vols. 3-4), NUREG-1715 Vols. 1-4, U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, Office of Nuclear Regulatory Research, April 2000, June 2000, July 2001 and September 2001

sources.name: NUREG/CR-6890 Vols. 1 and 2 (INL/EXT-05-00501) with the LOOP 2023 update (INL/RPT-24-79969)
sources.covers: Loss of offsite power frequencies by category and plant mode, recovery time distributions and non-recovery probabilities, emergency diesel generator reliability and CCF factors, and station blackout core damage results
sources.boundaryConvention: A LOOP is the simultaneous loss of offsite power to all safety buses of a unit that requires all emergency generators to start. Events are split into plant-centered, switchyard-centered, grid-related and weather-related LOOPs, with the main and station transformer high-voltage terminals and the point where lines leave the switchyard as the borders. Critical operation counts LOOPs with a reactor trip, and shutdown operation counts LOOPs while the unit is shut down. EDG failure modes follow the SPAR models: fail to start, fail to load and run for 1 h, fail to run after 1 h, and test or maintenance unavailability.
sources.failureCounting: LOOP events come from licensee event reports and are counted per unit for frequencies. Durations use the potential bus recovery time, counted once per site when several units are hit by one event. LOOPs without a reactor trip and partial LOOPs are not counted. EDG counts come from EPIX for 1998-2002 and from unplanned undervoltage demands in LERs for 1997-2003.
sources.quality: Frequencies are Jeffreys or constrained noninformative Bayesian updates, or empirical Bayes gamma distributions where plant or site variation was found. Recovery times are lognormal fits by matching moments. SBO core damage values are SPAR model point estimates and Monte Carlo uncertainty results. Volumes 1 and 2 are scanned pages, so values were read from the OCR text and checked against page images and internal identities.
sources.reference: S. A. Eide, C. D. Gentillon, T. E. Wierman and D. M. Rasmuson, NUREG/CR-6890 Vols. 1 and 2 (INL/EXT-05-00501), U.S. NRC and Idaho National Laboratory, December 2005. N. Johnson and Z. Ma, Analysis of Loss-of-Offsite-Power Events 2023 Update, INL/RPT-24-79969, Idaho National Laboratory, July 2024.
